title: introduce-policy-sanctuary-rbacv2-kms-residency-guardian
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add Policy Sanctuary service: enforces tenant KMS residency constraints, attaches immutable residency audit headers, and introduces operator-lease RBAC v2 flow. Backwards-compatible; opt-in gate via feature flag.
commit_summary: 3 contributors, 9 logical commits. Key commits: initial service scaffold; residency rule engine and policy DSL; KMS selector with region affinity; operator-lease RBAC flow; audit header enricher and tests; private-installer deployment manifest and docs.
description:
Motivation: Customers with strict data residency controls asked for a lightweight, auditable enforcement point that can accept requests from the serving runtime and assert KMS usage + tenant residency without changing existing request paths. This PR introduces 'Policy Sanctuary' — a small, high-availability service that validates per-request residency constraints, selects an allowed KMS provider/region, and issues a short-lived operator lease token used by downstream services to access tenant-scoped keys. The service also emits immutable residency audit headers that are appended to the audit pipeline to improve forensic traceability.

What changed (single-string description): - New service 'policy-sanctuary' with a compact policy DSL for residency rules (services/policy-sanctuary/policy/engine.go). - KMS allocator that chooses a CMK endpoint based on tenant claims, configured geofences, and configured provider preference; falls back to a configurable soft-fail policy that triggers controlled audit-only mode. - RBAC v2 'operator-lease' flow implemented: operator requests short-lived leases with limited scopes; leases are minted with proof-of-residency assertions and TTL enforcement (services/policy-sanctuary/rbac/lease_handler.go). - Audit enricher that attaches immutable X-Residency-Assertion and X-KMS-Provenance headers; these headers are HMAC-signed using the platform audit signing key to prevent tampering (internal/audit/enricher/enricher.go). - Integration tests exercising residency matches, KMS fallback, and lease revocation (tests/integration/policy-sanctuary/residency_e2e_test.go). - Private installer / Helm charts and docs to allow opt-in deployment in VPC/on-prem installs (deploy/private-installer/*, helm/policy-sanctuary/*). - Feature flag and rollout plan in pkg/config/feature_flags.yaml so the service can be enabled via staged rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests added for policy engine - [x] Integration tests for end-to-end residency flow - [x] Helm chart and private-installer manifest included - [x] Docs and playbook for incident runbooks included - [x] Security review requested and completed (Sofia Martinez)

Files changed: See changed_files list above for highlights; no changes to public API surfaces of the serving runtime. The runtime calls remain behind a feature flag and use the new operator-lease token when enabled.

Testing and CI: CI run green for unit and integration matrix on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Load-smoke test simulating 200rps ran in a k3s environment — acceptable P95 latency impact under controlled batch sizes. A single flake in the cache eviction test was traced to test timing and fixed.

Review conversation (high-level): - Liam Patel: "The residency DSL looks compact — can we add a lint that rejects overly-broad allow rules?" — Author: "Added rule-linter and unit tests; linter runs in CI." - Sofia Martinez: "Audit header signing needs key rotation considerations." — Author: "Added key identifier header and rotation test; documented KMS signing key rotation in docs." - Igor Volkov: "Operator lease revocation path isn't clear on race with in-flight requests." — Author: "Added lease revocation callback and TTL check in allocator; documented best-effort rollback semantics in playbook." - Security approves after clarifications; SRE requested a soft-fail mode for partial outages which was implemented.

Rollout plan: Feature flag default off. Staged rollout with canary in a single region, followed by 24h telemetry review (audit header rates, lease minting rate, allocation errors). If residency mismatches exceed 0.1% or latency impact at P95 > 50ms, rollback.

Backward compatibility: The serving runtime continues to operate without the sanctuary service. When enabled, requests include an operator lease token; services that do not recognize the token will ignore it. The audit enricher emits additional headers that downstream consumers can opt into.

Operational notes: - Responsible oncall: security-infra rotation week of rollout. - Telemetry: meters for lease_minted, lease_revoked, kms_allocation_hits, kms_allocation_fallbacks, residency_audit_headers_emitted. - Alerting: high fallback rate (>0.5%) and increased audit rejections.

Related work: ENG-4822 tracks RBAC v2 policy templates for operator leases; SUP-1192 is a partner request case.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approvals and green CI.
merge_outcome: merged after approvals and green CI
